question: Is served decode throughput practically equivalent within plus or minus 2 percent on the twelve specified cases?
measurement: Per-repetition aggregate decode = streams * 255 / (last response chunk - first response chunk). Median of two repetitions per cell per fresh server.
analysis_unit: Six paired log ratios of candidate/base per-run medians for each cell; requests, streams and repetitions are not independent sample units.
interval: exp(mean(log ratios) +/- t_critical * sample_sd(log ratios) / sqrt(6))
acceptance: All twelve per-cell confidence intervals wholly inside the bounds, complete fixed sample, and full token/output equality. The global decision is intersection-union; intervals are per-cell, not simultaneous intervals.
inference_limits: Paired t intervals assume independent approximately normal block log ratios. Six blocks give limited precision. This is practical equivalence on the tested checkpoint/settings, not exact timing equality or universal equivalence.
stopping_rule: Exactly six paired blocks; no early acceptance, no extra runs selected from interval width or direction, no replacement pairs. Any safety or exactness failure stops the experiment. Missing observations cannot qualify.
inconclusive_rule: Any interval overlapping a bound is inconclusive. An interval wholly outside the band is not equivalent; do not automatically call this a regression.
safety: Existing 6 GiB guard, 9 GiB reserve, 8192 context, two lanes, prompt cache zero. Restore and health-check production after every window, including failure or cancellation. Stop after the first OOM and do not continue later windows.
scope: The prior 64-token drafted/plain gate remains separate. New 256-token outputs are checked across repetitions, solo/concurrent, sides and blocks; no new 256-token plain equality claim. TTFT is descriptive, not an equivalence endpoint.
